signature.name: Gateway Arch
signature.detail: The Gateway Arch is St. Louis's defining symbol and the tallest man-made monument in the United States. Ride the tram to the top for sweeping views of the Mississippi River and downtown. Book tickets online in advance, especially on weekends, and go early to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Forest Park
signature.detail: Forest Park is a sprawling urban park larger than Central Park and home to several major attractions. It's perfect for a stroll, picnic, or visiting the zoo and museums. Enter from any side; the park is free and open daily.

signature.name: St. Louis Zoo
signature.detail: The St. Louis Zoo is consistently ranked among the best free zoos in the country. It houses diverse animals and offers educational exhibits. Admission is free, but special attractions cost extra; arrive early for parking.

signature.name: City Museum
signature.detail: The City Museum is a one-of-a-kind indoor playground made from repurposed industrial materials. It's a must-see for its whimsical tunnels, slides, and rooftop views. Wear comfortable shoes and be ready to climb; tickets are timed.

signature.name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis
signature.detail: This cathedral is renowned for its stunning mosaics, among the largest in the world. It's a peaceful place to admire art and architecture. Dress respectfully, and check opening hours as it's an active church.

signature.name: Missouri Botanical Garden
signature.detail: The Missouri Botanical Garden is a historic and beautiful garden with diverse plant collections and a Japanese garden. It's a great spot for relaxation and photography. Allow at least two hours; tickets can be purchased at the gate.

signature.name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery
signature.detail: Take a tour of the Anheuser-Busch Brewery to learn about beer-making and see the historic buildings. Tours often include samples. Book ahead and bring ID for the tasting.

signature.name: Cahokia Mounds
signature.detail: Cahokia Mounds is a UNESCO World Heritage site with ancient earthen mounds built by Native Americans. It offers a glimpse into pre-Columbian history. It's a short drive from downtown; wear walking shoes and bring water.
